abstract: Writing counterspeech that challenges online hate speech can be cognitively and emotionally demanding, whereas fully automated generation may weaken users' sense of voice and responsibility. We present an in-browser AI-assisted co-writing tool that enables users to contribute their own ideas and offers three editable suggestions generated by a large language model using dynamically retrieved hate speech-counterspeech examples from the Multitarget CONAN dataset. We evaluated the tool in an exploratory within-subject study with ten participants, complemented by think-aloud observations and semi-structured interviews with half of the participants. Participants wrote responses to three self-selected hate speech instances without assistance and then repeated the task with the tool. Final responses were subsequently peer-rated for empathy, non-toxicity, relevance, specificity, and persuasiveness. Participants evaluated the interface positively, and qualitative accounts linked user input, selection among alternatives, and small edits to perceived agency and responsibility. Assisted responses received higher descriptive mean ratings across all five proxies, with the largest difference for empathy. Mean composition time increased from 2.52 to 3.88 minutes. Qualitative findings further revealed a tension between empathy-oriented outputs and users' desire to express legitimate anger or direct disagreement. We contribute exploratory design guidance for treating AI-assisted counterspeech as deliberative co-writing rather than automated text production.

ur.tldr: 针对反仇恨言论写作的认知与情感负担，构建浏览器内人机协同写作工具，从CONAN数据集中动态检索示例并由LLM生成三条可编辑建议。十人参与的被试内研究表明，用户评价积极，辅助响应在共情、无毒、相关性、具体性和说服力上均高于未辅助版本，共情提升最显著但耗时由2.52增至3.88分钟；质性分析揭示共情导向输出与用户表达愤怒/反对意愿之间的张力。

title: In-Browser Human-AI Co-Writing for Counterspeech: An Exploratory User Study of Agency, Perceived Response Quality, and Time
title_zh: 浏览器内人-AI 反话共写：自主性、感知质量与时间的探索性用户研究
